claim.statement: Current terminal documentation says Teams and Enterprise administrators can set the maximum auto-execution level; team and user allowlists and denylists are combined, denylist entries take precedence, and a denied command requires approval rather than being represented as an unconditional block.

source.title: Terminal
source.locator: Team settings; allowlist and denylist merging; precedence

values: Cascade Teams or Enterprise command policy

limitations: A denylist match is documented as requiring approval, so the catalog does not treat it as a security sandbox or absolute execution prohibition.
unknowns: The account plan, administrator maximum, merged list contents, matching behavior and any user approvals are unknown.
